before: A default parameter is used when the caller omits that argument or supplies undefined. It is not used for null, zero or an empty string. This distinction preserves intentionally supplied values.

The final parameter ...items gathers remaining arguments into a new array. Rest must be last. In labelList(prefix = "Items", ...items), the first argument belongs to prefix and all later arguments become items.

items.join(",") returns a string containing the items separated by commas, without changing the array. Template interpolation turns the supplied prefix into text. This lesson accepts printable simple values; it does not validate a user-facing schema.
Implement labelList(prefix = "Items", ...items) returning prefix + ": " + the comma-joined items. Apply the default only for omitted/undefined prefix and preserve an empty prefix.
after:
A default parameter supplies a value when an argument is missing or is `undefined`.

It does not replace `null`, 0, or empty text. Those are supplied values.

`...items` is a rest parameter: it gathers the remaining arguments into a new array. It must be the final parameter.

In `labelList(prefix = "Items", ...items)`, the first argument is the label. The later arguments become the items.

`items.join(",")` makes text with commas between the items. It leaves the array unchanged.

The template turns the prefix into text too. This exercise uses simple values and does not check rules for a larger data format.

Return the prefix, `": "`, and the joined items. Use `"Items"` only for an omitted or undefined prefix.

Keep an empty prefix empty. With no items, the result still ends in a colon and space.
